text: The low whistle in the night
why: Julia describes a low, clear whistle heard in the night.

text: The last few nights before that night, about three in the morning: a low, clear whistle wakes Julia
why: Julia says that during the last few nights, about three in the morning, a low, clear whistle has awakened her.
Julia gives her own account of the whistle to Helen in the quoted conversation.

text: Who made the low whistle in the night?
why: Plain question raised by Julia asking whether Helen had whistled and not knowing its source.

text: Where did the whistle come from?
why: Julia says she cannot tell where it came from.
A repeated whistle at the same hour each night naturally raises the question of its purpose, without pointing at an answer.

text: What was the whistle for? — a signal to someone
why: A generic possibility for a whistle in the night, with gipsies camped on the grounds.

text: What was the whistle for? — to frighten Julia
why: A reasonable possibility given the household's menace and Julia being disturbed by it.

text: What was the whistle for? — to call an animal
why: The story has established Indian animals roaming the grounds, and whistling to call animals is common knowledge, so a reader has reason to consider it.

text: Why was the whistle heard only during the last few nights?
why: Julia speaks of it only during the last few nights, which makes the recent onset a natural question.

text: Why was the whistle heard only during the last few nights? — it had to do with the approaching wedding
id: q.why_whistle_began=it had to do with the approaching wedding
why: The approaching wedding has just been mentioned and falls in the same period, so the possibility is reasonable.

text: Why was the whistle heard only during the last few nights? — it had been going on before, and she had only just woken to it
id: q.why_whistle_began=it had been going on before, and she had only just woken to it
why: A plain alternative explanation for why she only recently noticed it, invented nothing about the story.

text: Who made the low whistle in the night? — Julia thought it might have come from the next room
why: Julia says it came perhaps from the next room, which bears on who made it.

text: Where did the whistle come from? — Julia thought it might have come from the next room
why: Julia says directly it came perhaps from the next room.
